title: Confused customer needs simpler explanations

transcript.content: I do not understand tax years.

In the UK, the tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April the following year. For example, the tax year 2026-27 starts on 6 April 2026 and ends on 5 April 2027. This means that any income earned during this period is reported in your tax return for that specific tax year. 

If you have any specific questions about tax years or how they affect your tax obligations, feel free to ask!
What is the UK tax year in simple words?

The UK tax year is a 12-month period used by the government to calculate your income tax. It starts on 6 April and ends on 5 April the following year. For example, the tax year 2026-27 runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. During this time, any income you earn is reported for tax purposes. 

If you have more questions about how it works, just let me know!
What is Self Assessment in simple words?

Self Assessment is a system used by HMRC for individuals to report their income and calculate their tax. If you earn money that isn't taxed automatically (like from self-employment or rental income), you need to fill out a tax return each year. This helps HMRC determine how much tax you owe. 

You usually submit your tax return online or on paper, and the deadlines vary depending on the method you choose. If you have more questions about Self Assessment, feel free to ask!
What is Making Tax Digital in simple words?

Making Tax Digital (MTD) is a government initiative aimed at making the tax system more efficient and easier to manage. It requires certain businesses, like self-employed individuals and landlords, to keep digital records of their income and expenses. Instead of submitting a tax return once a year, they must send updates to HMRC quarterly.

This change helps ensure that tax information is accurate and up-to-date. If you have any specific questions about MTD or how it might affect you, just let me know!
I am employed only — keep it simple — do I need either?

If you are only employed and your income is taxed through PAYE (Pay As You Earn), you typically do not need to file a Self Assessment tax return. However, if you have additional untaxed income, such as from self-employment or rental income, you may need to register for Self Assessment.

If you're unsure about your situation, feel free to ask!
